claim: A decline in exposure to commensal microbes and gastrointestinal helminths in developed countries has been linked to increased prevalence of allergic and autoimmune inflammatory disorders (the hygiene hypothesis).
source: For example, a decline in exposure to commensal microbes and gastrointestinal helminths in developed countries has been linked to increased prevalence of allergic and autoimmune inflammatory disorders (the hygiene hypothesis).
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to the hygiene hypothesis, which is established scientific knowledge in the field.

claim: Crowe et al., 2020 reported that treatment with a secreted glycoprotein from a parasitic nematode can protect against murine aging by induction of anti-inflammatory mechanisms.
source: Interestingly, Crowe et al., 2020 recently reported that treatment with a secreted glycoprotein from a parasitic nematode can protect against murine aging by induction of anti-inflammatory mechanisms.
evidence: This claim is directly supported by citation to Crowe et al., 2020 study.

claim: The aging process is the main cause of senescent multimorbidity, the co-occurrence of multiple chronic pathologies that includes the major diseases of late life.
source: The aging process is the main cause of senescent multimorbidity, the co-occurrence of multiple chronic pathologies that includes the major diseases of late life.
evidence: This claim represents established knowledge in geroscience.

claim: Inflammaging is a state of systemic, low-grade inflammation that increases with age, independent of attack by infectious pathogens.
source: While there are clearly multiple contributory factors, one determinant whose importance is becoming increasingly clear is inflammaging, the state of systemic, low-grade inflammation that increases with age, independent of attack by infectious pathogens (Franceschi et al., 2000).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Franceschi et al., 2000, which introduced the concept of inflammaging.

claim: Inflammaging is a contributory factor in diverse age-related pathologies, including cardiovascular disease, dementia, cancer, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), osteoporosis, and age-related macular degeneration.
source: Such inflammation is a contributory factor in diverse age-related pathologies, including cardiovascular disease, dementia, cancer, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), osteoporosis, age-related macular degeneration (Xia et al., 2016), and perhaps even symptom severity during SARS-CoV-2 (COVID-19) infections (Akbar and Gilroy, 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Xia et al., 2016 and Akbar and Gilroy, 2020.

claim: Inflammaging may contribute to symptom severity during SARS-CoV-2 (COVID-19) infections.
source: Such inflammation is a contributory factor in diverse age-related pathologies, including cardiovascular disease, dementia, cancer, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), osteoporosis, age-related macular degeneration (Xia et al., 2016), and perhaps even symptom severity during SARS-CoV-2 (COVID-19) infections (Akbar and Gilroy, 2020).
evidence: The use of 'perhaps even' indicates this is speculative, though supported by citation to Akbar and Gilroy, 2020.

claim: One cause of inflammaging is gut dysbiosis, an imbalance in the composition of the intestinal microbiome.
source: One cause of inflammaging is gut dysbiosis, an imbalance in the composition of the intestinal microbiome.
evidence: This claim represents established knowledge in the field of aging research.

claim: Gut dysbiosis can manifest as loss of immunomodulatory microbial species and is exacerbated by pro-dysbiotic aspects of the modern lifestyle, including antibiotic usage and the so-called Western diet.
source: Such imbalance can manifest as loss of immunomodulatory microbial species and is exacerbated by pro-dysbiotic aspects of the modern lifestyle, including antibiotic usage and the so-called Western diet (Buford, 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Buford, 2017.

claim: The 'old friends' hypothesis argues that the human immune system evolved optimal function in a dirtier world, including the presence of various microbes and helminth parasites, whose removal leads to pathogenic immunological hyperactivity.
source: One interpretation of the cause of such dysbiotic effects utilizes the 'old friends' hypothesis (derived from the hygiene hypothesis [Strachan, 1989]). This argues that the human immune system evolved optimal function in a dirtier world, including the presence of various microbes and helminth parasites, whose removal leads to pathogenic immunological hyperactivity (Rook et al., 2004).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Strachan, 1989 and Rook et al., 2004.

claim: Gut dysbiosis contributes to allergic and autoimmune inflammation prior to aging.
source: Gut dysbiosis certainly does contribute to allergic and autoimmune inflammation prior to aging (Kamada et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Kamada et al., 2013.

claim: Fecal microbiota transfer from healthy donors has been suggested as a potential anti-inflammaging therapy.
source: Indeed, fecal microbiota transfer from healthy donors has been suggested as a potential anti-inflammaging therapy (Franceschi and Campisi, 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Franceschi and Campisi, 2014.

claim: Parasitic helminths have infected humans throughout their evolutionary history.
source: Parasitic helminths have infected humans throughout their evolutionary history.
evidence: This claim represents established knowledge in evolutionary biology and parasitology.

claim: Helminths have become master manipulators of the human immune system in order to dodge host attack.
source: As a consequence, helminths have become master manipulators of our immune system in order to dodge host attack.
evidence: This claim represents established knowledge in parasitology.

claim: Humans have evolved some levels of tolerance of helminth presence.
source: Meanwhile, we have evolved some levels of tolerance of their presence.
evidence: This claim is based on evolutionary reasoning and established knowledge.

claim: Elephantiasis can result from overly aggressive anti-helminth responses to infection with the filarial nematode Wuchereria bancrofti.
source: The wisdom of sometimes putting up with helminths is illustrated by the pathologies that can result from overly aggressive anti-helminth responses, as in elephantiasis that can result from infection with the filarial nematode Wuchereria bancrofti (Figure 1a).
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to Figure 1a and represents established medical knowledge.

claim: Normal human immune development and function is likely to have become dependent upon the presence of immunomodulatory helminths, as well as that of their microbial counterparts.
source: Through such coevolution, normal human immune development and function is likely to have become dependent upon the presence of immunomodulatory helminths, as well as that of their microbial counterparts (Velasquez-Manoff, 2012).
evidence: This claim is speculative but supported by citation to Velasquez-Manoff, 2012 and evolutionary reasoning.

claim: Reduced helminth infection in ultra-clean modern societies has been linked to increased rates of allergic and autoimmune inflammatory disease.
source: Indeed, like old friend microbes, reduced helminth infection in ultra-clean modern societies has been linked to increased rates of allergic and autoimmune inflammatory disease, while restorative helminth therapies can protect against these conditions (see next section).
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to evidence discussed in the next section of the manuscript.

claim: Restorative helminth therapies can protect against allergic and autoimmune inflammatory disease.
source: Indeed, like old friend microbes, reduced helminth infection in ultra-clean modern societies has been linked to increased rates of allergic and autoimmune inflammatory disease, while restorative helminth therapies can protect against these conditions (see next section).
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to evidence discussed in the next section of the manuscript.

claim: A variety of inflammatory disorders that afflict people prior to aging have been linked to a loss of old friend helminths, including asthma, atopic eczema, inflammatory bowel disease, multiple sclerosis (MS), rheumatoid arthritis, and type 1 diabetes.
source: A variety of inflammatory disorders that afflict people prior to aging have been linked to a loss of old friend helminths. These include asthma, atopic eczema, inflammatory bowel disease, multiple sclerosis (MS), rheumatoid arthritis, and type 1 diabetes (Maizels, 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Maizels, 2020.

claim: A study from Argentina found that accidental acquisition of helminth infections caused a reduction in inflammatory cytokines and alleviated disease symptoms in MS patients.
source: For example, a study from Argentina found that accidental acquisition of helminth infections not only caused a reduction in inflammatory cytokines, but also alleviated disease symptoms in MS patients, and that clearance of parasites reversed these effects (Correale and Farez, 2007; Correale and Farez, 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Correale and Farez, 2007 and 2011.

claim: Clearance of helminth parasites reversed the reduction in inflammatory cytokines and alleviation of MS symptoms.
source: For example, a study from Argentina found that accidental acquisition of helminth infections not only caused a reduction in inflammatory cytokines, but also alleviated disease symptoms in MS patients, and that clearance of parasites reversed these effects (Correale and Farez, 2007; Correale and Farez, 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Correale and Farez, 2007 and 2011.

claim: Studies from Uganda found that hookworm infections in pregnant women confer protection against infantile atopic eczema.
source: In a similar vein, studies from Uganda found that hookworm infections in pregnant women confer protection against infantile atopic eczema, protection that is abrogated by anthelmintic treatment during pregnancy (Mpairwe et al., 2011; Mpairwe et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Mpairwe et al., 2011 and 2014.

claim: Anthelmintic treatment during pregnancy abrogates the protection against infantile atopic eczema conferred by hookworm infections.
source: In a similar vein, studies from Uganda found that hookworm infections in pregnant women confer protection against infantile atopic eczema, protection that is abrogated by anthelmintic treatment during pregnancy (Mpairwe et al., 2011; Mpairwe et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Mpairwe et al., 2011 and 2014.

claim: J.E. Turton reported in 1976 in The Lancet that maintaining an infection with the intestinal hookworm Necator americanus alleviated his allergies.
source: More directly, a number of studies have documented beneficial effects of deliberate helminth infections, beginning with J.E. Turton's 1976 report in The Lancet, which describes how maintaining an infection with the intestinal hookworm Necator americanus alleviated his allergies (Turton, 1976).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Turton, 1976.

claim: To date, 20 studies of the autoimmune encephalomyelitis mouse model of MS have reported helminth-induced reductions in disease severity.
source: For example, to date, 20 studies of the autoimmune encephalomyelitis mouse model of MS have reported helminth-induced reductions in disease severity (Charabati et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Charabati et al., 2020.

claim: Some initial clinical trials of T. suis ova therapy to treat patients with inflammatory bowel disease yielded promising results.
source: However, although some initial clinical trials of T. suis ova therapy to treat patients with inflammatory bowel disease yielded promising results (Elliott and Weinstock, 2017), follow-up trials have not thus far (Huang et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Elliott and Weinstock, 2017.

claim: Follow-up trials of T. suis ova therapy to treat patients with inflammatory bowel disease have not yielded promising results.
source: However, although some initial clinical trials of T. suis ova therapy to treat patients with inflammatory bowel disease yielded promising results (Elliott and Weinstock, 2017), follow-up trials have not thus far (Huang et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Huang et al., 2018.

claim: There is evidence that treatment with N. americanus hookworms is beneficial against celiac disease, an autoimmune disease affecting the bowel.
source: A possibility here is that only true old friends (i.e. anthropophilic helminths) will provide therapeutic benefits; notably, there is evidence that treatment with N. americanus hookworms is beneficial against celiac disease, an autoimmune disease affecting the bowel (Croese et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Croese et al., 2015.

claim: Administration of the glycoprotein ES-62 secreted by the rodent filarial nematode Acanthocheilonema viteae can recapitulate many of the immunomodulatory changes resulting from filarial infections.
source: For example, administration of the glycoprotein ES-62 secreted by the rodent filarial nematode Acanthocheilonema viteae can recapitulate many of the immunomodulatory changes resulting from filarial infections and is protective in several pathological contexts (Figure 1c).
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to Figure 1c and represents established knowledge from prior research.

claim: ES-62 is protective in several pathological contexts.
source: For example, administration of the glycoprotein ES-62 secreted by the rodent filarial nematode Acanthocheilonema viteae can recapitulate many of the immunomodulatory changes resulting from filarial infections and is protective in several pathological contexts (Figure 1c).
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to Figure 1c.

claim: A variety of helminth-derived proteins are protective in rodent models of MS.
source: Similarly, a variety of helminth-derived proteins are protective in rodent models of MS (Dixit et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Dixit et al., 2017.

claim: Inflammaging can be detected as a sterile, persistent elevation of pro-inflammatory molecules in the blood, including cytokines such as IL-6 and TNF-α and acute phase proteins such as C-reactive protein (CRP).
source: Inflammaging can be detected as a sterile, persistent elevation of pro-inflammatory molecules in the blood, including cytokines such as IL-6 and TNF-α and acute phase proteins such as C-reactive protein (CRP).
evidence: This claim represents established knowledge in the field of aging research.

claim: Reduced levels of circulating pro-inflammatory cytokines and CRP have been seen in people infected by strongylid and filarial helminths in a number of studies.
source: Interestingly, reduced levels of circulating pro-inflammatory cytokines and CRP have been seen in people infected by strongylid and filarial helminths in a number of studies (Aravindhan et al., 2010; George et al., 2014; Rajamanickam et al., 2019; Rajamanickam et al., 2020) (though not all [Aravindhan et al., 2012]), and experimental helminth infection similarly reduces pro-inflammatory cytokines in human serum (Gaze et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to multiple studies (Aravindhan et al., 2010; George et al., 2014; Rajamanickam et al., 2019; Rajamanickam et al., 2020; Gaze et al., 2012), though the authors note not all studies found this (Aravindhan et al., 2012).

claim: Experimental helminth infection reduces pro-inflammatory cytokines in human serum.
source: Interestingly, reduced levels of circulating pro-inflammatory cytokines and CRP have been seen in people infected by strongylid and filarial helminths in a number of studies (Aravindhan et al., 2010; George et al., 2014; Rajamanickam et al., 2019; Rajamanickam et al., 2020) (though not all [Aravindhan et al., 2012]), and experimental helminth infection similarly reduces pro-inflammatory cytokines in human serum (Gaze et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Gaze et al., 2012.

claim: Expulsion of helminths by anthelmintic medication induces elevated pro-inflammatory cytokine responsiveness in human blood.
source: Furthermore, expulsion of helminths by anthelmintic medication induces elevated pro-inflammatory cytokine responsiveness in human blood (Bourke et al., 2013; Wammes et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Bourke et al., 2013 and Wammes et al., 2016.

claim: ES-62 is a 62 kDa glycoprotein found in the excretory secretory products of the filarial nematode parasite A. viteae with anti-inflammatory properties.
source: ES-62 is a 62 kDa glycoprotein found in the excretory secretory products of the filarial nematode parasite A. viteae with anti-inflammatory properties.
evidence: This claim represents established knowledge about ES-62.

claim: Crowe et al., 2020 reported that weekly administration of ES-62 improved late-life health and increased lifespan (+12%, median lifespan) in a C57BL/6J mouse model of high-calorie diet-accelerated aging.
source: In the first study of its kind, Crowe et al., 2020 reported that weekly administration of ES-62 improved late-life health and increased lifespan (+12%, median lifespan) in a C57BL/6J mouse model of high-calorie diet-accelerated aging.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Crowe et al., 2020.

claim: Administration of ES-62 prevented the age-related decline in gut barrier integrity seen in high-calorie diet-accelerated aging.
source: Administration of ES-62 prevented the age-related decline in gut barrier integrity seen in high-calorie diet-accelerated aging (Crowe et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Crowe et al., 2020.

claim: Permeabilization of the gut lining can contribute to inflammaging, by allowing foreign antigens to leak into the blood and induce systemic immune activation.
source: Of interest in the present context is that permeabilization of the gut lining can contribute to inflammaging, by allowing foreign antigens to leak into the blood and induce systemic immune activation (Thevaranjan et al., 2017; Ferrucci and Fabbri, 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Thevaranjan et al., 2017 and Ferrucci and Fabbri, 2018.

claim: ES-62 prevented and, to some extent, even reversed age-related decreases in Bacteroidetes:Firmicutes ratio and increases in Proteobacteria in the gut.
source: Indeed, ES-62 prevented and, to some extent, even reversed age-related decreases in Bacteroidetes:Firmicutes ratio and increases in Proteobacteria in the gut (Crowe et al., 2020), both of which are associated with inflammaging (Fransen et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Crowe et al., 2020.

claim: Age-related decreases in Bacteroidetes:Firmicutes ratio and increases in Proteobacteria in the gut are associated with inflammaging.
source: Indeed, ES-62 prevented and, to some extent, even reversed age-related decreases in Bacteroidetes:Firmicutes ratio and increases in Proteobacteria in the gut (Crowe et al., 2020), both of which are associated with inflammaging (Fransen et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Fransen et al., 2017.

claim: IL-22 is an essential cytokine for maintaining gut barrier integrity.
source: Another possible mode of action is helminth-induced production of IL-22, an essential cytokine for maintaining gut barrier integrity (Sonnenberg et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Sonnenberg et al., 2011.

claim: The intestinal murine roundworm Heligmosomoides polygyrus can induce fetal-like reversion in intestinal cells to effect tissue repair.
source: Interestingly, the intestinal murine roundworm Heligmosomoides polygyrus can even induce fetal-like reversion in intestinal cells to effect tissue repair (Nusse et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Nusse et al., 2018.

claim: Administration of ES-62 prevented adipocyte hypertrophy in gonadal visceral fat.
source: Administration of ES-62 also prevented adipocyte hypertrophy in gonadal visceral fat (Crowe et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Crowe et al., 2020.

claim: Adiposity is a major source of inflammaging.
source: This, again, is notable given that adiposity is a major source of inflammaging.
evidence: This claim represents established knowledge in the field of aging research.

claim: Adipose tissue, particularly visceral fat, is highly infiltrated by immune cells, such as monocytes, B and T lymphocytes, mast cells, and neutrophils.
source: Adipose tissue, particularly visceral fat, is highly infiltrated by immune cells, such as monocytes, B and T lymphocytes, mast cells, and neutrophils, and is also a major site of senescent cell accumulation (Tchkonia et al., 2010; Mraz and Haluzik, 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Tchkonia et al., 2010 and Mraz and Haluzik, 2014.

claim: Adipose tissue is a major site of senescent cell accumulation.
source: Adipose tissue, particularly visceral fat, is highly infiltrated by immune cells, such as monocytes, B and T lymphocytes, mast cells, and neutrophils, and is also a major site of senescent cell accumulation (Tchkonia et al., 2010; Mraz and Haluzik, 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Tchkonia et al., 2010 and Mraz and Haluzik, 2014.

claim: Adipocytes, immune cells, and senescent cells in adipose tissue secrete a potent and destructive cocktail of pro-inflammatory molecules, including TNF-α, IL-6, IFN-γ, and leptin, which enter systemic circulation and contribute to the inflammaging phenotype.
source: Together, these adipocytes, immune cells, and senescent cells secrete a potent and destructive cocktail of pro-inflammatory molecules, including TNF-α, IL-6, IFN-γ, and leptin, which enter systemic circulation and contribute to the inflammaging phenotype.
evidence: This claim represents established knowledge in the field of aging research.

claim: ES-62 administration reduced the decline in eosinophil number in visceral fat.
source: In line with this, ES-62 administration reduced the decline in eosinophil number in visceral fat (Crowe et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Crowe et al., 2020.

claim: Nippostrongylus brasiliensis, a gastrointestinal roundworm of rodents, reduces adiposity apparently by reducing intestinal glucose absorption through altered STAT6 signaling.
source: Nippostrongylus brasiliensis, a gastrointestinal roundworm of rodents, reduces adiposity apparently by reducing intestinal glucose absorption through altered STAT6 signaling (Moyat et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Moyat et al., 2019.

claim: One study of humans reported an inverse correlation between previous schistosome infection and central obesity, though adjustment for socio-economic status was not performed.
source: One study of humans reported an inverse correlation between previous schistosome infection and central obesity, though adjustment for socio-economic status was not performed (Shen et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Shen et al., 2015, though the authors note a limitation of the study.

claim: Experimental helminth infection or treatment with helminth antigens can protect against pathology in the collagen-induced arthritis (CIA) and MRL/lpr mouse models of rheumatoid arthritis.
source: Indeed, experimental helminth infection or treatment with helminth antigens can protect against pathology in the collagen-induced arthritis (CIA) and MRL/lpr mouse models of rheumatoid arthritis (Smallwood et al., 2017; Langdon et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Smallwood et al., 2017 and Langdon et al., 2019.

claim: ES-62-mediated protection against CIA was accompanied by reduced serum levels of the pro-inflammatory cytokine IL-17.
source: Notably, ES-62-mediated protection against CIA was accompanied by reduced serum levels of the pro-inflammatory cytokine IL-17 (Pineda et al., 2012), consistent with protection against systemic inflammation.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Pineda et al., 2012.

claim: In a region of Eastern India endemic for lymphatic filariasis infection, not one of 207 rheumatoid arthritis patients tested positive for circulating filarial nematode antigens, while 40% of 222 healthy controls were antigen positive.
source: For example, in a region of Eastern India endemic for lymphatic filariasis infection, it was found that not one of 207 rheumatoid arthritis patients tested positive for circulating filarial nematode antigens; by contrast, 40% of 222 healthy controls were antigen positive (Panda et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Panda et al., 2013.

claim: Several epidemiological studies have reported an inverse relationship between the incidence of helminth infection and type 2 diabetes.
source: Several (but not all [Mendonça et al., 2006]) epidemiological studies have reported an inverse relationship between the incidence of helminth infection and type 2 diabetes (Aravindhan et al., 2010; Chen et al., 2013; Hays et al., 2015), and also serum levels of the pro-inflammatory cytokines IL-6 and GM-CSF (Aravindhan et al., 2010); these studies controlled for age and body mass index (and/or income).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Aravindhan et al., 2010; Chen et al., 2013; Hays et al., 2015, though the authors note not all studies found this (Mendonça et al., 2006).

claim: Epidemiological studies have reported an inverse relationship between helminth infection and serum levels of the pro-inflammatory cytokines IL-6 and GM-CSF.
source: Several (but not all [Mendonça et al., 2006]) epidemiological studies have reported an inverse relationship between the incidence of helminth infection and type 2 diabetes (Aravindhan et al., 2010; Chen et al., 2013; Hays et al., 2015), and also serum levels of the pro-inflammatory cytokines IL-6 and GM-CSF (Aravindhan et al., 2010); these studies controlled for age and body mass index (and/or income).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Aravindhan et al., 2010.

claim: Experimental helminth infections protected mice from type 2 diabetes-associated states such as hyperglycemia and insulin resistance.
source: And again, experimental helminth infections protected mice from type 2 diabetes-associated states such as hyperglycemia and insulin resistance (Wu et al., 2011; Morimoto et al., 2016; Pace et al., 2018), while anthelmintic treatment elevated blood glucagon and insulin resistance, and several circulating pro-inflammatory cytokines (Tahapary et al., 2017; Rajamanickam et al., 2019; Rajamanickam et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Wu et al., 2011; Morimoto et al., 2016; Pace et al., 2018.

claim: Anthelmintic treatment elevated blood glucagon and insulin resistance, and several circulating pro-inflammatory cytokines.
source: And again, experimental helminth infections protected mice from type 2 diabetes-associated states such as hyperglycemia and insulin resistance (Wu et al., 2011; Morimoto et al., 2016; Pace et al., 2018), while anthelmintic treatment elevated blood glucagon and insulin resistance, and several circulating pro-inflammatory cytokines (Tahapary et al., 2017; Rajamanickam et al., 2019; Rajamanickam et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Tahapary et al., 2017; Rajamanickam et al., 2019; Rajamanickam et al., 2020.

claim: The burden of Opisthorchis felineus (cat liver fluke) in cadavers was found to be negatively correlated with the severity of aortic atherosclerosis.
source: Regarding atherosclerosis, the burden of Opisthorchis felineus (cat liver fluke) in cadavers was found to be negatively correlated with the severity of aortic atherosclerosis (Magen et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Magen et al., 2013.

claim: Infection with the blood fluke Schistosoma mansoni reduced atherosclerotic lesions by 50% in atherosclerotic mouse models.
source: In atherosclerotic mouse models, infection with the blood fluke Schistosoma mansoni reduced atherosclerotic lesions by 50% (Doenhoff et al., 2002); similarly, administration of Schistosoma egg antigens reduced atherosclerotic plaque size (Zhang et al., 2012; Wolfs et al., 2014), and ES-62 reduced atherosclerotic lesion area by 60% in the gld.apoE−/− mouse model of lupus-accelerated atherosclerosis (Aprahamian et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Doenhoff et al., 2002.

claim: Administration of Schistosoma egg antigens reduced atherosclerotic plaque size.
source: In atherosclerotic mouse models, infection with the blood fluke Schistosoma mansoni reduced atherosclerotic lesions by 50% (Doenhoff et al., 2002); similarly, administration of Schistosoma egg antigens reduced atherosclerotic plaque size (Zhang et al., 2012; Wolfs et al., 2014), and ES-62 reduced atherosclerotic lesion area by 60% in the gld.apoE−/− mouse model of lupus-accelerated atherosclerosis (Aprahamian et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Zhang et al., 2012 and Wolfs et al., 2014.

claim: ES-62 reduced atherosclerotic lesion area by 60% in the gld.apoE−/− mouse model of lupus-accelerated atherosclerosis.
source: In atherosclerotic mouse models, infection with the blood fluke Schistosoma mansoni reduced atherosclerotic lesions by 50% (Doenhoff et al., 2002); similarly, administration of Schistosoma egg antigens reduced atherosclerotic plaque size (Zhang et al., 2012; Wolfs et al., 2014), and ES-62 reduced atherosclerotic lesion area by 60% in the gld.apoE−/− mouse model of lupus-accelerated atherosclerosis (Aprahamian et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Aprahamian et al., 2015.

claim: The tapeworm Taenia crassiceps and its antigens have been found to attenuate and prevent colon tumorigenesis in mice through anti-inflammatory mechanisms.
source: The tapeworm Taenia crassiceps and its antigens have been found to attenuate and prevent colon tumorigenesis in mice through anti-inflammatory mechanisms (León-Cabrera et al., 2014; Callejas et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to León-Cabrera et al., 2014 and Callejas et al., 2019.

claim: The nematode H. polygyrus was found to promote tumorigenesis in a mouse model of colon cancer.
source: However, in the same mouse model, the nematode H. polygyrus was found to promote tumorigenesis (Pastille et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Pastille et al., 2017.

claim: The trematode parasite Schistosoma haematobium causes bladder cancer.
source: Moreover, certain parasitic helminths are well known to increase cancer rates, for example the trematode parasite Schistosoma haematobium causes bladder cancer (Vennervald and Polman, 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Vennervald and Polman, 2009.

claim: Some helminths are known to suppress lung inflammation and to reduce levels of the pro-inflammatory cytokine IL-33, a driver of COPD pathology.
source: This includes COPD, given that some helminths are known to suppress lung inflammation and to reduce levels of the pro-inflammatory cytokine IL-33, a driver of COPD pathology (Osbourn et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Osbourn et al., 2017.

claim: N. brasiliensis can promote COPD pathology.
source: It should be noted however that other helminths such as N. brasiliensis can promote COPD pathology (Marsland et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Marsland et al., 2008.

claim: IL-33 promotes age-related macular degeneration.
source: Meanwhile, IL-33 also promotes age-related macular degeneration (Xi et al., 2016), another late-life inflammaging-linked disease.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Xi et al., 2016.

claim: Anecdotal evidence from home-users of live helminth therapy suggests that old friend helminths may provide protection against Parkinson's disease and depression.
source: Anecdotal evidence from home-users of live helminth therapy suggests that old friend helminths may also provide protection against Parkinson's disease and depression, although whether the latter includes geriatric depression is not known (Cheng et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Cheng et al., 2015, though the authors note it is anecdotal evidence.

claim: Both Parkinson's disease and geriatric depression are considered to be inflammaging-linked conditions.
source: Both Parkinson's disease and geriatric depression are considered to be inflammaging-linked conditions (Teixeira et al., 2012; Calabrese et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Teixeira et al., 2012 and Calabrese et al., 2018.

claim: There is clear evidence that an absence of helminth infection leads to increased incidence of inflammatory disorders, including some inflammaging-linked conditions, such as rheumatoid arthritis.
source: There is clear evidence that an absence of helminth infection leads to increased incidence of inflammatory disorders, including some inflammaging-linked conditions, such as rheumatoid arthritis.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the evidence presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: Experimental and clinical work has demonstrated the protective benefits of restorative helminth therapy against some inflammaging-linked diseases.
source: Furthermore, experimental and clinical work has demonstrated the protective benefits of restorative helminth therapy against some inflammaging-linked diseases.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the evidence presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: ES-62 extended lifespan in male, but not female obese mice.
source: Here it is notable that ES-62 extended lifespan in male, but not female obese mice (Crowe et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Crowe et al., 2020.

claim: The pro-aging mTOR pathway was found to be inhibited in human dendritic cells by Brugia malayi microfilariae.
source: A further possibility is that helminths might inhibit tissue aging in their hosts in order to protect their local niche; notably, the pro-aging mTOR pathway was found to be inhibited in human dendritic cells by Brugia malayi microfilariae (Narasimhan et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Narasimhan et al., 2016.

claim: Improvements in hygiene and elimination of helminth parasites have been of incalculable benefit to humanity.
source: It goes without saying that improvements in hygiene and elimination of helminth parasites have been of incalculable benefit to humanity.
evidence: This claim represents established knowledge and common understanding.

claim: A cost coupled with improvements in hygiene is abnormalities of immune function, specifically inflammatory hyperfunction.
source: But a cost coupled with this benefit is abnormalities of immune function, specifically inflammatory hyperfunction.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the old friends hypothesis and evidence presented in the manuscript.

claim: Available evidence suggests that restorative helminth therapies are effective against not only allergic and autoimmune inflammatory disorders, but also age-associated inflammation in later life, at least to some extent.
source: Available evidence suggests that restorative helminth therapies are effective against not only allergic and autoimmune inflammatory disorders, but also age-associated inflammation in later life, at least to some extent.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the evidence presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: Helminth therapy could provide protection against the wide spectrum of age-related diseases promoted by inflammaging.
source: Should this be confirmed, helminth therapy could provide protection against the wide spectrum of age-related diseases promoted by inflammaging.
evidence: This claim is speculative, contingent on confirmation of the anti-inflammaging effects of helminth therapy.

claim: Helminths can prevent gut dysbiosis, a known contributor to inflammaging.
source: Indeed, ES-62 prevented and, to some extent, even reversed age-related decreases in Bacteroidetes:Firmicutes ratio and increases in Proteobacteria in the gut (Crowe et al., 2020), both of which are associated with inflammaging (Fransen et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is inferred from the evidence that ES-62 prevented age-related changes in gut microbiome composition associated with inflammaging.

claim: The extended lifespan observed with ES-62 treatment was likely due to suppression of intestinal changes that contribute to inflammaging.
source: Thus, it is plausible that the extended lifespan was due to suppression of intestinal changes that contribute to inflammaging.
evidence: This claim is speculative, based on inference from the observed effects of ES-62 on gut barrier integrity and microbiome composition.

claim: Helminth therapy might be of particular benefit to people who are overweight or obese.
source: More generally, given the relationship between adiposity and inflammaging, helminth therapy might be of particular benefit to people who are overweight or obese.
evidence: This claim is speculative, based on inference from the relationship between adiposity and inflammaging and the observed effects of helminths on adiposity.

claim: Helminth therapy could act in a preventative fashion, delaying the genesis or worsening of inflammaging-linked pathologies.
source: Would helminth therapy act only in a preventative fashion (typical of anti-aging treatments), delaying the genesis or worsening of inflammaging-linked pathologies, or could it reverse existing disease symptoms?
evidence: This claim is speculative, posed as a question for future research.

claim: Helminth therapy could potentially reverse existing disease symptoms.
source: At least for murine rheumatoid arthritis, there is some evidence that helminth therapy could be both prophylactic and therapeutic (McInnes et al., 2003; Rzepecka et al., 2015). Thus, it is possible that helminth therapy could, to some extent, reverse symptoms of aging as well as decelerate them.
evidence: This claim is speculative but supported by citations to McInnes et al., 2003 and Rzepecka et al., 2015 showing therapeutic effects in rheumatoid arthritis.

claim: Helminths could counter inflammaging by inhibiting sources of inflammaging such as preventing gut barrier permeabilization and obesity.
source: For example, they could inhibit sources of inflammaging by preventing gut barrier permeabilization and obesity, neutralize existing inflammaging by increasing the proportion of anti-inflammatory to pro-inflammatory cytokines, or repair inflammaging-afflicted tissue damage, for example through promotion of IL-22 secretion (Figure 2b).
evidence: This claim is speculative, based on inference from observed effects of helminths and reference to Figure 2b.

claim: Helminths could counter inflammaging by neutralizing existing inflammaging through increasing the proportion of anti-inflammatory to pro-inflammatory cytokines.
source: For example, they could inhibit sources of inflammaging by preventing gut barrier permeabilization and obesity, neutralize existing inflammaging by increasing the proportion of anti-inflammatory to pro-inflammatory cytokines, or repair inflammaging-afflicted tissue damage, for example through promotion of IL-22 secretion (Figure 2b).
evidence: This claim is speculative, based on inference from observed effects of helminths and reference to Figure 2b.

claim: Helminths could counter inflammaging by repairing inflammaging-afflicted tissue damage through promotion of IL-22 secretion.
source: For example, they could inhibit sources of inflammaging by preventing gut barrier permeabilization and obesity, neutralize existing inflammaging by increasing the proportion of anti-inflammatory to pro-inflammatory cytokines, or repair inflammaging-afflicted tissue damage, for example through promotion of IL-22 secretion (Figure 2b).
evidence: This claim is speculative, based on inference from observed effects of helminths and reference to Figure 2b.

claim: Helminths might inhibit tissue aging in their hosts in order to protect their local niche.
source: A further possibility is that helminths might inhibit tissue aging in their hosts in order to protect their local niche; notably, the pro-aging mTOR pathway was found to be inhibited in human dendritic cells by Brugia malayi microfilariae (Narasimhan et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is speculative but supported by citation to Narasimhan et al., 2016 showing mTOR pathway inhibition.

claim: Elephantiasis results from infection with the filarial nematode Wuchereria bancrofti.
source: The wisdom of sometimes putting up with helminths is illustrated by the pathologies that can result from overly aggressive anti-helminth responses, as in elephantiasis that can result from infection with the filarial nematode Wuchereria bancrofti (Figure 1a).
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to Figure 1a and represents established medical knowledge.

claim: In a mouse model of high-calorie diet-accelerated aging, ES-62 administration prevented age-associated increases in gut permeability and adiposity, and increased longevity.
source: In addition, in a mouse model of high-calorie diet-accelerated aging, ES-62 administration prevented age-associated increases in gut permeability and adiposity, and increased longevity (Crowe et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by Figure 1c caption and citation to Crowe et al., 2020.

claim: Helminth therapy has been demonstrated to protect against early- and mid-onset disorders by controlling pre-aging inflammation.
source: Helminth therapy has been demonstrated to protect against early- and mid-onset disorders by controlling pre-aging inflammation, but whether it can also protect against mid- and late-onset disorders through anti-inflammaging mechanisms remains uncertain.
evidence: This claim is supported by Figure 2a caption and represents a summary of evidence presented in the manuscript.

claim: Whether helminth therapy can protect against mid- and late-onset disorders through anti-inflammaging mechanisms remains uncertain.
source: Helminth therapy has been demonstrated to protect against early- and mid-onset disorders by controlling pre-aging inflammation, but whether it can also protect against mid- and late-onset disorders through anti-inflammaging mechanisms remains uncertain.
evidence: This claim is explicitly stated in Figure 2a caption as uncertain.

claim: MS (age of onset 20–50 years) and lupus (15–45 years) are sometimes described as inflammaging related.
source: We note that MS (age of onset 20–50 years) and lupus (15–45 years) are sometimes described as inflammaging related (Sanai et al., 2016; Musella et al., 2018; Tsai et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by Figure 2a caption and citations to Sanai et al., 2016; Musella et al., 2018; Tsai et al., 2019.

claim: Helminth therapy could target the inflammatory source and/or mediator and/or the damaged tissues.
source: Helminth therapy could in principle target the inflammatory source and/or mediator and/or the damaged tissues.
evidence: This claim is supported by Figure 2b caption and represents speculation about potential mechanisms.

claim: The geroscience approach views preventative intervention in the aging process as a means to simultaneously pre-empt the development of multiple age-related diseases.
source: The geroscience approach views preventative intervention in the aging process as a means to simultaneously pre-empt the development of multiple age-related diseases (Austad, 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Austad, 2016.

claim: Trichuris suis does not reproduce in humans.
source: However, these concerns may be assuaged by controlling dose size and using helminths with different definitive hosts, such as the pig whipworm Trichuris suis which does not reproduce in humans (Figure 1b).
evidence: This claim represents established knowledge about T. suis biology.

claim: Only true old friends (i.e. anthropophilic helminths) may provide therapeutic benefits.
source: A possibility here is that only true old friends (i.e. anthropophilic helminths) will provide therapeutic benefits; notably, there is evidence that treatment with N. americanus hookworms is beneficial against celiac disease, an autoimmune disease affecting the bowel (Croese et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is speculative, based on inference from the differential results with T. suis vs N. americanus.

claim: Long-lasting, low-level helminth infections might represent cheaper and more efficient forms of therapy than helminth-derived proteins.
source: However, long-lasting, low-level helminth infections might still represent cheaper and more efficient forms of therapy, providing the full panoply of immunomodulatory agents and in a form that is easy to administer; c.f. ES-62 that was given in weekly injections (Crowe et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is speculative, based on inference about practical considerations of therapy administration.

claim: Helminth therapy currently shows promise as a means to treat inflammatory conditions such as allergy and autoimmunity.
source: Taken together, helminth therapy currently shows promise as a means to treat inflammatory conditions such as allergy and autoimmunity (Figure 2a).
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the evidence presented throughout the manuscript.
